literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) describe the same set of C-terminal fusion constructs: OX1R-Rluc, OX1R-nRluc, OX1R-cRluc, and OX1R-nYFP. L2 states explicitly that the receptor cDNA was subcloned 'to be in-frame with restriction sites of pRluc-N1, pEYFP-N1, nYFP-pcDNA3.1, cYFP-pcDNA3.1, nRluc-pcDNA3.1 and cRluc-pcDNA3.1 vectors to provide plasmids that express proteins fused to the C-terminal end.' The authoritative topology landmarks place the HCRTR1 C-terminus (residues 362–425) in the INTRACELLULAR compartment. L4 confirms that the OX1R-Rluc fusion protein reaches the plasma membrane (surface display of the receptor is intact), but the Rluc/YFP tag itself faces the cytoplasm. No ledger line reports a tag on the extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–44), in any extracellular loop (ECL1: 109–116; ECL2: 183–213; ECL3: 325–337), or at any other extracellular position. Because the ledger contains no qualifying extracellular insertion, zero sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Rluc/nRluc/cRluc/nYFP fusions are appended after the last residue (P425) of OX1R; the C-terminus (residues 362–425) is intracellular per topology, so these tags face the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
